scope: Fail-closed capability taxonomy derived from the inspected GitHub, GitLab, and Gerrit public contracts; not a claim of provider-wide equivalence

states.name: INTENT_HEAD_BOUND
states.meaning: The effect request is bound to an exact reviewed source/head or patch-set revision.
states.not_enough_for: Does not prove request acceptance, queue admission, or final repository effect.

states.name: SERVER_OPERATION_ID_BOUND
states.meaning: A server-assigned durable/recoverable operation identifier is tied to the requested work.
states.not_enough_for: Does not prove that the operation completed or what target-ref commit resulted.

states.name: QUEUE_OR_TRAIN_ADMITTED
states.meaning: Server has admitted the change into asynchronous queue/train processing.
states.not_enough_for: Does not prove final branch effect.

states.name: CI_STATE_BOUND
states.meaning: A pipeline/check execution is bound to the queue/train candidate state.
states.not_enough_for: Pipeline/check SHA can be a synthetic merge-group/train state and must not be assumed to be the final target-ref SHA.

states.name: FINAL_TARGET_REF_EFFECT_EXACT
states.meaning: The exact protected/target ref transition that actually landed has been observed and durably recorded.
states.not_enough_for: Does not by itself prove which policy path or bypass allowed the effect.

states.name: POST_EFFECT_POLICY_EXACT
states.meaning: Server-derived policy/submit evidence is exact-read and bound to the landed effect or the submitted group.
states.not_enough_for: Provider semantics still matter; pass, bypass, override and evaluate-only states must remain distinct.

github.SERVER_OPERATION_ID_BOUND: async merge UUID; 409 recovery requires pending option comparison
github.CI_STATE_BOUND: merge-group/check-run evidence; merge-group SHA is queue-group state, not final base SHA
github.POST_EFFECT_POLICY_EXACT: Rule Suite exact tuple/id readbacks; result pass vs bypass and evaluation_result separated
github.recovery_caveat: async result endpoint explicitly expires after 24h; persist UUID/terminal response immediately

gitlab.INTENT_HEAD_BOUND: merge-train add sha or merge-request merge sha
gitlab.CI_STATE_BOUND: train pipeline id/SHA/status; pipeline can be canceled/recreated when earlier cars change
gitlab.FINAL_TARGET_REF_EFFECT_EXACT: merged MR attribution plus exact target-branch ref evidence; merge_commit_sha/squash_commit_sha are merge-method-sensitive
gitlab.POST_EFFECT_POLICY_EXACT: train pipeline outcome plus merged MR state; this taxonomy does not claim a GitHub-Rule-Suite-equivalent per-ref policy object
gitlab.recovery_caveat: inspected API exposes active and complete train scopes and does not state a GitHub-style 24h expiry; no indefinite-retention claim

gerrit.INTENT_HEAD_BOUND: POST /changes/{change-id}/revisions/{revision-id}/submit addresses one exact patch-set revision
gerrit.SERVER_OPERATION_ID_BOUND: ChangeInfo.submission_id is set on MERGED changes and identifies changes submitted together; callers must not rely on its string format
gerrit.QUEUE_OR_TRAIN_ADMITTED: not modeled as a merge queue in the inspected Gerrit submit contract; submit directly executes Gerrit submit semantics
gerrit.CI_STATE_BOUND: submit requirements / plugin submit rules are evaluated server-side, but a pre-submit requirement snapshot is not a reusable effect lease
gerrit.FINAL_TARGET_REF_EFFECT_EXACT: must still read the destination ref because Gerrit submit type may merge, rebase, fast-forward or cherry-pick and can create a commit different from the reviewed revision
gerrit.POST_EFFECT_POLICY_EXACT: MERGED ChangeInfo + submission_id + submit-requirement/override provenance when preserved; historical ChangeInfo can be addressed by NoteDb meta SHA
gerrit.recovery_caveat: submission may include topic/dependent closure; capture Submitted Together/member closure and submission_id, not only the triggering change

cross_provider_invariants: Pre-effect authorization or policy-read evidence is never promoted into a reusable lease unless the effect API itself atomically consumes that exact revision/epoch.
Expected-head/revision binding and server operation identity are independent evidence axes.
Queue/train admission and CI success are not final target-ref effect.
Final effect is proven against the target repository ref, not a synthetic merge-group/train pipeline SHA.
Group operations require a durable ordered/member closure; a single triggering PR/MR/change is insufficient when the server may submit multiple members.
Post-effect policy states must preserve bypass/override/evaluate-only distinctions instead of collapsing them into green/pass.
Ambiguous mutation responses are recovered by exact operation/intention readback before any retry.
